extracted.intended_audience: peer reviewers for the Yale Journal of Biology and Medicine (YJBM)
extracted.subtask_description: Checklist-style guidance for peer reviewers assessing manuscripts submitted to the Yale Journal of Biology and Medicine, with article-type specific criteria for Original Research, Case Reports, Reviews, and Perspectives/Analyses/Profiles/Interviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interest to YJBM readers
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the article of interest to YJBM readers?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General criterion for all submissions; reviewers should judge topical relevance and likely reader engagement for the journal's audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify strengths and weaknesses
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General: note major and minor strengths and limitations across the manuscript to inform editorial decisions and suggested revisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial collaboration opportunities
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine how editors can collaborate with authors for improvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General: point out ways editors might help authors (e.g., scope, clarity, structure) rather than only recommending rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity of overall research aim and stated findings
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarity of overall research aim and stated findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original Research: assess whether the paper clearly communicates its objectives and what it found.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract quality regarding aims and results
rubrics_metrics.description: Abstract quality regarding aims and results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original Research (also emphasized for Reviews/Case Reports): verify the abstract concisely and accurately summarizes aims and main results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficiency of background information
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original Research: check that the introduction and background provide adequate context and rationale for the study for readers unfamiliar with the topic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence quality supporting claims
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original Research: evaluate whether data and analyses substantiate the authors' claims; identify unsupported assertions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgment of similar published work
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original Research: ensure authors cite and discuss closely related studies and position their contribution relative to existing literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data quality and analytical correctness
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original Research (and Case Reports): check raw data quality, sample size/selection issues, appropriate statistical methods, and correct interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness of figures and tables
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original Research (and Reviews/Case Reports): assess whether figures/tables are necessary, clear, correctly labeled, and add value to the text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology clarity for reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original Research: verify that methods are described in sufficient detail for others to reproduce the work or understand limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment between conclusions and data
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original Research and Case Reports: ensure conclusions are supported by presented data, avoiding overreach or unsupported speculation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discussion of implications with balanced literature review
rubrics_metrics.description: Discussion of implications with balanced literature review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original Research: check that authors situate findings within the literature and discuss implications and limitations in a balanced way.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility for unfamiliar readers
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied across Original Research, Case Reports, Reviews: the manuscript should be readable and comprehensible to YJBM readers who may not be specialists in the narrow subfield.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper abbreviation explanation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original Research: confirm that abbreviations are defined on first use and used consistently to aid readability for non-specialists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Case report abstract clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Abstract clarity on aim, findings, implications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Case Reports: abstract should succinctly present the case's aim, key findings, and their implications for clinical practice or understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Case report introduction accessibility
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Case Reports: background/introduction should make the clinical context understandable to readers who are not specialists in that condition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear case presentation description
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Case Reports: the patient's presentation, investigations, treatments, and course should be presented clearly, chronologically, and with necessary detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Case report figure and table clarity and utility
rubrics_metrics.description: Figure and table clarity and utility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Case Reports: visual elements should illustrate key clinical findings or data and be labeled/legible for clinical interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Case report accurate data analysis and reporting
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Case Reports: ensure any analyses are appropriate and that reported clinical data are accurate and complete (e.g., labs, timelines).

rubrics_metrics.name: Case report conclusion alignment with presented data
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Case Reports: conclusions should be cautious and directly linked to the single case or small case series presented, avoiding broad generalizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Case report discussion of similar cases and treatment relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Discussion of similar cases and treatment relevance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Case Reports: authors should compare the case with previously published cases and discuss implications for diagnosis or management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review accessibility for unfamiliar YJBM readers
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews: ensure the review is written so non-experts in the narrow area can follow the narrative and appreciate the review's value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review abstract accuracy
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews: abstract must accurately reflect the review's scope, main conclusions, and any recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review clear introduction focus
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews: introduction should define the review question/scope and explain why the topic is important or timely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review factual accuracy throughout
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews: check for correct representation of cited studies, avoidance of factual errors, and precise language when summarizing evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review utilization of recent literature
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews: assess whether the review incorporates up-to-date studies and relevant recent developments in the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review logical organization with subheadings
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews: the structure should be logical, with subheadings that guide the reader through themes, methods, or topical sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review balanced perspectives on debated topics
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews: ensure the review fairly represents differing viewpoints and does not unduly favor one interpretation without justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review relevant figures and tables
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews: visual elements should synthesize evidence (e.g., summary tables, conceptual figures) and aid reader comprehension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review forward-looking conclusions addressing research gaps
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews: conclusions should identify open questions and recommend directions for future research or practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perspectives/Analyses/Profiles/Interviews checklist items
rubrics_metrics.description: Each article type has its own checklist (abstract accuracy, contextual background, balanced viewpoints, logical conclusions, lessons learned).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For Perspectives, Analyses, Profiles, Interviews: ensure abstracts are accurate, context/background is provided, viewpoints are balanced, conclusions are logical, and clear lessons or takeaways are offered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common cross-type criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Common throughout: abstract conciseness, accessibility, logical conclusions, balanced treatment, helpful organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply these criteria across all article types: abstracts should be concise; manuscripts should be accessible to non-specialists; conclusions must follow logically from the body; treatment of topics should be balanced; organization should help reader navigation.
